_comment: WO-598 vendor/shops REGISTRY - the per-vendor STOCK QUERY (the honest shelf). Loaded by DeNelle.Village.VendorRegistry via DeNelle.Core.CanonicalJson (Resources first, StreamingAssets fallback). Each vendor's shelf is a QUERY over the item catalogs (weapons/armor/accessories/consumables/materials), never a hardcoded list: 'categories' names which catalog bands the vendor stocks, 'classFilter':'roster' drops items no CURRENTLY-PLAYABLE class can use (the playable set is DeNelle.Core.State.PlayableHeroes -> no Mage wands at the Forge while ff.knightonly is ON), 'maxReqLevel' (0 = uncapped) tier-gates the shelf, and 'emptyLine' is the AUTHORED never-raw empty-state line. WO-860 adds the THINNED-shelf knobs (onlyEquippable / perLevelCap / excludeIdPrefixes / footerLine) so the store retunes as DATA with no recompile. VendorStockContract.AllowedFor consults this registry FIRST (categories -> GearKind flags) so the legacy shop, the MVVM PartyShop, ShopCatalog and the AutoPilot oracle all read ONE truth.

_schemaNotes.id: vendor/structure id (buildings.json isShoppable id, the vendorContext DialogueService.PlayStructure routes). Matched exact first, then substring (so 'blacksmith_forge' finds 'forge').
_schemaNotes.layout: gear | goods | jeweler - which shelf PRESENTATION the shop binds (gear = weapons/armor + party fit; goods = flat consumables/materials list, no equip context; jeweler = rings/amulets/gems).
_schemaNotes.categories: weapon | armor | consumable | material | ring | amulet | accessory | gem | craftable - the catalog bands this vendor's query pulls.
_schemaNotes.classFilter: roster (default: only items obtainable by the current playable roster - Knight-only under ff.knightonly) | none.
_schemaNotes.maxReqLevel: 0 = uncapped; N = don't stock items requiring level > N (tier gate). Level-locked rows still SHOW as 'Requires Lv N' unless onlyEquippable is true.
_schemaNotes.emptyLine: authored 'come back later' line shown when the query resolves 0 items - a vendor never renders a raw empty grid.
_schemaNotes.onlyEquippable: WO-860. true = HIDE rows the shopper cannot equip right now (wrong class / under-level) instead of listing them LOCKED. false/absent = the pre-860 aspiration shelf. Reuses the EXISTING equip gate (WeaponFitsClass / ArmorFitsClass / req.level) as the show-filter - the gate is correct, only its consequence changes.
_schemaNotes.perLevelCap: WO-860. Max weapon/armor rows stocked PER REQUIRED LEVEL (owner: 'only 2 options on each new level'). 0/absent = uncapped. WHICH rows survive is a documented deterministic sort in VendorStockResolver.EmitCapped: bucket by req.level, then power DESCENDING (damageMult for weapons, defense for armor), tie-broken by id ORDINAL ASCENDING so the pick never depends on catalog row order, locale or device.
_schemaNotes.excludeIdPrefixes: WO-860. Item-id prefixes this vendor never stocks (case-insensitive). 'blink_' keeps the ~65 art-pack placeholder rows off the player-facing shelf WITHOUT editing the catalogs (they stay ownable/equippable). Empty/absent = stock everything.
_schemaNotes.footerLine: WO-860. The 'come back after leveling for new stock' line rendered UNDER a NON-EMPTY capped list - the case a player hits most once perLevelCap is on (they have wares; better ones unlock later). Distinct from emptyLine, which covers 0 results. Absent = render no footer.
_schemaNotes.lockedPreviewLevels: WO-960 (owner: 'display as greyed out with lvl and only show ones in the next 5 levels'). N > 0 = a class-appropriate row locked ONLY by level still SHOWS, greyed + non-purchasable with its 'Lv N' requirement, when req.level is within the shopper's next N levels (req in (level, level+N]); deeper future rows stay hidden. Under onlyEquippable this RE-ADMITS the near-future ladder slice; on the aspiration shelf it CLAMPS level-locked rows to the same window. 0/absent = pre-960 behaviour exactly.

vendors._excludeIdPrefixesNote: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and deliberately DIFFERENT from the armorer's ['blink_'] - this is a ruling, not drift. WO-860 (2026-08-02) asked for the blink_ exclusion on both shelves and only the armorer got it; the owner then RATIFIED the WO-500 damage curve on all 65 blink_ WEAPON rows and unhid them (2026-08-14, 'apply the ratified WO-500 curve to the 65 and unhide them'), which makes them shelf CONTENT rather than art-pack placeholders. The armorer keeps its exclusion for the opposite reason: blink ARMOR is junked (ff.blinkarmor OFF, pivot 2026-06-22). Pinned by ForgeShelfClassKindRegression case 3 - if this list ever changes, change this note in the SAME edit or the suite goes red.
